answers.quote: More than half of the total forest land has been declared reserved forests. Reserved forests are regarded as the most valuable as far as the conservation of forest and wildlife resources are concerned.

answers.quote: India has a network of 1014 Protected Areas including 106 National Parks, 573 Wildlife Sanctuaries, 115 Conservation Reserves and 220 Community Reserves covering a total of 1,75,169.42 km2 of geographical area of the country which is approximately 5.32%.

answers.quote: Madhya Pradesh has the largest area under permanent forests, constituting 75 per cent of its total forest area.
answers.notes: MP has largest permanent forest area, 75%.

answers.answer: সরকারি ও বেসরকারি ব্যক্তি-সম্প্রদায়ের মালিকানাধীন অন্যান্য বন ও পতিত জমি
answers.quote: These are other forests and wastelands belonging to both government and private individuals and communities.
answers.notes: Definition matches c15 verbatim.

answers.answer: পাঠ্যবইয়ের সংখ্যাটি বই ছাপার সময়ের হিসাব; সংরক্ষিত এলাকার জাল পরে আরও বেড়েছে বলে হালনাগাদ ডেটাবেসে সংখ্যা বেশি
answers.quote: India has a network of 1014 Protected Areas including 106 National Parks, 573 Wildlife Sanctuaries, 115 Conservation Reserves and 220 Community Reserves covering a total of 1,75,169.42 km2 of geographical area of the country which is approximately 5.32%.

answers.notes: Statement 1 from c14 (~one-third protected); statement 2 from c13 (reserved most valuable). Both true.

answers.quote: When we conserve and protect the whole ecosystem, its biodiversity at all levels is protected - we save the entire forest to save the tiger. This approach is called in situ (on site) conservation.
answers.notes: Saving entire forest to save tiger is in situ per c22.

answers.quote: Zoological parks, botanical gardens and wildlife safari parks serve this purpose.
answers.notes: Zoological parks serve ex situ purpose per c27.

answers.quote: Initially 25 biodiversity hotspots were identified but subsequently nine more have been added to the list, bringing the total number of biodiversity hotspots in the world to 34.
answers.notes: 25 + 9 more = 34 hotspots.

answers.answer: পশ্চিমঘাট ও শ্রীলঙ্কা, ইন্দো-বর্মা এবং হিমালয়
answers.quote: Three of these hotspots – Western Ghats and Sri Lanka, Indo-Burma and Himalaya – cover our country’s exceptionally high biodiversity regions.
answers.notes: Three hotspots listed in c25.

answers.answer: বাণিজ্যিকভাবে গুরুত্বপূর্ণ উদ্ভিদের বিভিন্ন জিন-ধারার বীজ দীর্ঘদিনের জন্য
answers.quote: Now gametes of threatened species can be preserved in viable and fertile condition for long periods using cryopreservation techniques, eggs can be fertilised in vitro, and plants can be propagated using tissue culture methods. Seeds of different genetic strains of commercially important plants can be kept for long periods in seed banks.
answers.notes: Seed banks keep seeds of genetic strains of commercially important plants.

answers.answer: প্রজাতি বিপন্ন হয়ে বন্য পরিবেশে অদূর ভবিষ্যতে বিলুপ্তির উচ্চ ঝুঁকিতে থাকলে এবং জরুরি ব্যবস্থা দরকার হলে
answers.quote: However, when there are situations where an animal or plant is endangered or threatened (organisms facing a very high risk of extinction in the wild in the near future) and needs urgent measures to save it from extinction, ex situ (off site) conservation is the desirable approach.
answers.notes: Ex situ desirable when endangered/threatened and urgent measures needed.

answers.quote: Such sacred groves are found in Khasi and Jaintia Hills in Meghalaya, Aravalli Hills of Rajasthan, Western Ghat regions of Karnataka and Maharashtra and the Sarguja, Chanda and Bastar areas of Madhya Pradesh.
answers.notes: Pairs 1 (Khasi/Jaintia, Meghalaya) and 3 (Sarguja/Chanda/Bastar, MP) match c29; pair 2 wrong - Rajasthan site is Aravalli Hills, not Thar.

answers.quote: "Project Tiger", one of the wellpublicised wildlife campaigns in the world, was launched in 1973.
answers.notes: Project Tiger launched 1973.

answers.quote: Corbett National Park in Uttarakhand, Sunderbans National Park in West Bengal, Bandhavgarh National Park in Madhya Pradesh, Sariska Wildlife Sanctuary in Rajasthan, Manas Tiger Reserve in Assam and Periyar Tiger Reserve in Kerala are some of the tiger reserves of India.
answers.notes: Sunderbans NP in West Bengal per c10.

answers.quote: In 1973, the authorities realised that the tiger population had dwindled to 1,827 from an estimated 55,000 at the turn of the century.
answers.notes: Tiger population dwindled to 1,827 in 1973.

answers.answer: বাঘের জন্য অতিরিক্ত সংরক্ষিত এলাকা ঘোষণা
answers.quote: The major threats to tiger population are numerous, such as poaching for trade, shrinking habitat, depletion of prey base species, growing human population, etc.
answers.notes: Threats in c07 are poaching, shrinking habitat, prey depletion, growing population; extra PAs not listed.

answers.quote: The central government also announced several projects for protecting specific animals, which were gravely threatened, including the tiger, the onehorned rhinoceros, the Kashmir stag or hangul, three types of crocodiles – fresh water crocodile, saltwater crocodile and the Gharial, the Asiatic lion, and others.
answers.notes: Kashmir stag or hangul in c05.

answers.answer: শুধু বিপন্ন প্রজাতি বাঁচানো নয়, বড় মাত্রার জীব-অঞ্চল (biotype) সংরক্ষণ
answers.quote: Tiger conservation has been viewed not only as an effort to save an endangered species, but with equal importance as a means of preserving biotypes of sizeable magnitude.
answers.notes: Preserving biotypes of sizeable magnitude per c09.

answers.quote: Corbett National Park in Uttarakhand, Sunderbans National Park in West Bengal, Bandhavgarh National Park in Madhya Pradesh, Sariska Wildlife Sanctuary in Rajasthan, Manas Tiger Reserve in Assam and Periyar Tiger Reserve in Kerala are some of the tiger reserves of India.
answers.notes: Corbett-Uttarakhand, Bandhavgarh-MP, Manas-Assam, Periyar-Kerala per c10.

answers.quote: Biosphere Reserves are areas of terrestrial and coastal / marine ecosystems or a combination thereof, which are internationally recognized within the framework of UNESCO’s flagship programme on Man and Biosphere (MAB)
answers.notes: Recognised within UNESCO MAB framework per c41.

answers.quote: Sundarban Wetland in West Bengal, designated on 30 January 2019, is India’s largest Ramsar Site at 4,23,000 hectares.
answers.notes: Sundarban Wetland largest Ramsar site per c51.

answers.quote: the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change has, as on December 2023, established 18 Biosphere Reserves.
answers.notes: 18 BRs as on Dec 2023 per c43.

answers.answer: চিলিকা হ্রদ ও কেওলাদেও জাতীয় উদ্যান
answers.quote: Chilika Lake in Odisha and Keoladeo National Park in Rajasthan became India’s first Ramsar Sites on 1 October 1981.
answers.notes: Chilika and Keoladeo first Ramsar sites per c50.

answers.quote: It was adopted at Ramsar, Iran, on 2 February 1971 and entered into force in 1975.
answers.notes: Adopted at Ramsar, Iran, 2 Feb 1971 per c47.

answers.answer: যেসব রামসার স্থানের বাস্তুতান্ত্রিক চরিত্র বদলেছে, বদলাচ্ছে বা বদলানোর আশঙ্কা আছে, তাদের নথি (register)
answers.quote: It is a register of Ramsar Sites where changes in ecological character have occurred, are occurring or are likely to occur.
answers.notes: Montreux Record definition matches c55.

answers.notes: A from c42 (humans integral component); R also supported by c46 (livelihood support in buffer/transition reduces core pressure) and explains A.

answers.notes: Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980 per c34.

answers.answer: যে কোনো এলাকাকে অভয়ারণ্য, জাতীয় উদ্যান বা বদ্ধ এলাকা ঘোষণা করার ক্ষমতা
answers.quote: It empowers the central and state governments to declare any area a wildlife sanctuary, national park or closed area. The Act prohibits hunting of animals except with permission of authorized officer when animal has become dangerous to human life or property or so disabled or diseased as to be beyond recovery.
answers.notes: Power to declare sanctuary/NP/closed area per c33.

answers.answer: শিকার নিষিদ্ধ করা, আবাসকে আইনি সুরক্ষা দেওয়া, বন্যপ্রাণীর বাণিজ্য সীমিত করা
